[[Reykjavík]] | capacity = 1,215 | chairman = Oscar Clausen | manager = Ólafur Hrannar Kristjánsson | league = [[1. deild karla (football)|1. deild karla]] | season = [[2025 1. deild karla|2025]] | position = 1. deild karla, 9th of 12 | website = https://www.leiknir.com/ | pattern_la1 =_leiknir2021h | pattern_b1 =_leiknir2021h | pattern_ra1 =_leiknir2021h | pattern_sh1 = | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = 0000FF | body1 = af071d | rightarm1 = 0000FF | shorts1 = 0a1e51 | socks1 = 0a1e51 | pattern_la2 =_leiknir2021a | pattern_b2 =_leiknir2021a | pattern_ra2 =_leiknir2021a | pattern_sh2 =_leiknir2021a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF }} '''Íþróttafélagið Leiknir''' ({{IPA|is|ˈiːˌθrouhtaˌfjɛːˌlaijɪð ˈleiknɪr̥}}, {{lit|Leiknir Sports Club}}{{efn|''Íþróttafélagið'' is the [[Definiteness|definite form]] of ''Íþróttafélag'', meaning "the sports club".}}), commonly known as '''Leiknir Reykjavík''' ({{IPA|is|ˈleiknɪr̥ ˈreiːcaˌviːk}}), is an Icelandic [[multi-sport club]]. It is best known for its men's [[association football|football]] section, but also fields departments in [[Badminton]], [[Basketball]], [[Volleyball]] and [[Karate]].{{cite web |title=Leiknir Reykjavík – Stolt Breiðholts |url=https://www.leiknir.com/ |website=leiknir.com |publisher=Íþróttafélagið Leiknir |access-date=6 February 2023 |language=Icelandic}} The club was founded in 1973 and is based in [[Breiðholt]] neighbourhood of [[Reykjavík]]. Leiknir plays its home matches at [[Leiknisvöllur]], which has a capacity of 1,215 of which 525 seating{{cite web | url=https://www.ksi.is/mannvirki/vellir/knattspyrnuvellir/vollur/?vollur=62 | title=Leiknisvöllur - Knattspyrnusamband Íslands }} The club's motto is ''"Pride of Breiðholt"''."}}
